This implies a potential indirect mechanism where Phenylbutazone influences Cyp2c9 via its interaction with these transporters and their subsequent binding to substrates. The lowest common ancestors of these interactions—Nonsteroidal Antiinflammatory Drugs and Organic Molecules—highlight the broader context of the drug's molecular profile. The scores from the paths indicate a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, suggesting that the interaction may be significant but not definitive. The integration of these pathways underscores the role of transporters in modulating enzyme activity, offering a plausible mechanism for the observed effects.
